etymologies.etymologyHTML: Probably from Middle French pistole, or via Middle English pistolet, from Middle French pistolet (“small firearm or small dagger”). The origin is unclear, if via German to Romance probably from Middle High German forms like pischulle from Czech píšťala (“firearm”, literally “tube, pipe”), from Proto-Slavic *piščalь, from *piskati, *piščati (“to squeak, whistle”), from Proto-Balto-Slavic *pīṣk-. Alternatively, if from Romance to German, from or related to Italian pistolese (“short dagger”), from Italian Pistoia (“a Tuscan town noted for its gunsmithing”).

definitions.definition: The mechanical component of a fuse in a bomb or torpedo responsible for firing the detonator.
A creative and unpredictable jokester, a constant source of entertainment and surprises.

quote.citation: 2011, Diane Lierow, Bernie Lierow, Kay West, Dani's Story: A Journey from Neglect to Love‎[1], page 81:
quote.text: She was gregarious, opinionated, and in charge, the kind of person you'd describe as a real pistol, and I was immediately drawn to her.

quote.citation: February 2012, Thomas Pugsley, Denial (episode) in Young Justice (TV series):
quote.text: KENT NELSON —Until my wife Inza convinced me there was more to life. Ah, she was a real pistol, that Inza.

quote.citation: 2012, Jimmy Correa, How My Prank Stories in ‘You Tube’ Made Me an Overnight Sensation, iUniverse, page 102:
quote.text: She features so many dance tunes and is a pistol with her sharp and witty remarks.

definitions.definition: (Southern US) A small boy who is bright, alert and very active.
(American football) An offensive formation in which the quarterback receives the snap at a distance behind the center, but closer than in a shotgun formation, with a running back lined up behind him.
(transitive) To shoot (at) a target with a pistol.
